_comment: Tests the always-on 'How to Discover Context' rule doc-this installs. Configs are with_rule / without_rule (the rule block present/absent in the staged CLAUDE.md), NOT with_skill/without_skill. Each case is a read-only question answered against the staged corpus. grade.py reads answer_keywords (AND-of-ORs, case-insensitive), answer_forbidden (none may appear), process, target_file, and tool_budget. process is one check or a list of checks (all must pass): readme_first | agents_first | fallback_file. agents_first asserts the nearest AGENTS.md (= target_file) was read before any content access — AGENTS.md is the per-folder instructions artifact and its nearest-lookup is independent of README's.

evals.name: retry-policy-value
evals.prompt: What is the billing service's payment retry policy? State the number of attempts and the backoff strategy.
evals.expected_output: 3 attempts with exponential backoff. The value is stated in services/billing/README.md and configured in services/billing/settings.py (RETRY_ATTEMPTS=3, RETRY_BACKOFF=exponential). The README-first path reads billing/README.md and answers directly; a blind grep for 'retry' also surfaces legacy_config.py (5 attempts, fixed) and risks reporting the stale value.

evals.name: notify-naming-convention
evals.prompt: What naming convention do events emitted by the notify service follow? Give the format.
evals.expected_output: The platform-wide format <service>.<entity>.<action> (lowercase, dot-separated, three parts), e.g. notify.email.sent. It is defined once in services/README.md; notify/README.md points up to it. Answering requires walking up from the notify service to the parent services README.

evals.name: billing-source-of-truth
evals.prompt: Which file holds the source-of-truth configuration for the billing service's retry behavior?
evals.expected_output: services/billing/settings.py. The billing README names settings.py as authoritative and explicitly flags legacy_config.py as deprecated/no-longer-loaded. A blind grep for retry config surfaces both files; without reading the README an agent can wrongly name legacy_config.py.

evals.name: ops-script-purpose
evals.prompt: What does ops/scripts/rotate-keys.sh do? Summarize its purpose.
evals.expected_output: It rotates the API signing keys: generates a new signing key, publishes it to the key store, marks the previous key as retiring (valid 24h), then revokes keys older than 24h; runs weekly via cron. ops/scripts/ has NO README, so the correct behavior is to fall back to reading the script directly rather than hunting for documentation that does not exist.

evals.name: subfolder-agents-no-readme
evals.prompt: In the auth service (services/auth/), how should I add a new token type?
evals.expected_output: Edit services/auth/token_types.yaml and run `python gen_tokens.py` to regenerate tokens.py. tokens.py is generated and must not be hand-edited. services/auth/ has its own AGENTS.md (the binding rule) but NO README, so the two discovery artifacts resolve independently: the nearest AGENTS.md is services/auth/AGENTS.md (the subfolder's) while the nearest README is the parent services/README.md. An agent that never reads the subfolder AGENTS.md cannot name token_types.yaml + the generator and would wrongly suggest editing tokens.py.

evals.name: payments-refund-constraint
evals.prompt: How should application code in the payments service issue a refund?
evals.expected_output: By calling request_refund(charge_id), which enqueues the refund for approval — never by calling refund() directly (that bypasses fraud review; only the approval worker calls refund()). services/payments/ has BOTH a README and an AGENTS.md; the README describes refunds and names refund() as the low-level reversal, but the binding rule lives only in services/payments/AGENTS.md. An agent that reads just the README (or treats README/CLAUDE.md as sufficient) wrongly answers refund(); reading the subfolder AGENTS.md is required.

evals.name: auth-handlers-agents-walkup
evals.prompt: I'm working in services/auth/handlers/refresh.py and need a new token type it can use. How should that token type be defined?
evals.expected_output: Edit services/auth/token_types.yaml and run `python gen_tokens.py` to regenerate tokens.py — never hand-edit tokens.py. services/auth/handlers/ has no AGENTS.md of its own, so the binding rule must be found by walking UP to the nearest parent AGENTS.md at services/auth/AGENTS.md (the mirror of walking up for a README). An agent that doesn't walk up misses the generated-file rule.
